belief: Christians shouldn't get depressed or anxious.
origins: Many churches speak of joy and peace without space for struggle. Believers who feel depressed or anxious may think they are failing, or that they are not truly saved.
teaches: David wrote, “Why are you downcast, O my soul? Why the unease within me? Put your hope in God.” Elijah wanted to die, and God cared for him. Jesus was “a man of sorrows, acquainted with grief,” and in Gethsemane He said, “My soul is consumed with sorrow to the point of death” (Matthew 26:38). Paul wrote of being “hard pressed on all sides.” Depression and anxiety can have many causes, including biology, loss, stress, and trauma. They are not signs of unbelief, and help is available.
self_statements: I should be able to pray this away.
Others will think less of me.
errors: Believing a Christian is either joyful or faithless.
Predicting that I will never be okay.
Feeling low and concluding my faith is false.
questions: Who taught me that Christians do not feel this way?
Which biblical figures struggled with sadness or fear?
What does my body and life situation contribute?
What help have I sought: doctor, counselor, friends, pastor?
What does Scripture say about God’s nearness to the downcast?
truth: Depression and anxiety are not failures of faith. Many faithful people have struggled. God is near, and help through counseling, medical care, and community is part of His provision.
log: Each week, note one step of care and one truth.
actions: If thoughts of self-harm come, call or text 988 (U.S.).
prayer: Lord, I am weighed down. Meet me in my sadness and fear, send help, and let me know You are near. Amen.
